{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — IBM e-business Hosting Agreement (Bluefly)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and negotiation priorities  
**Position:** We represent the Customer (Bluefly).

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Seven clauses are compliant and require no redline, including the areas that most often cause problems for us on the buy side: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment and no non-solicitation binding us, and § 14.16 (Freedom of Action) affirmatively preserves our right to contract with other suppliers. Governing law is New York, our preferred choice, with no arbitration clause; the only shortfall is silence on venue, which we note rather than redline.

Eleven rules are deviations and one (transition assistance) is missing entirely. The concentration of risk is on **exit and remedy**: our termination-for-convenience right in § 3.4 is conditioned on uncapped early termination charges with no refund of prepaid Charges (§ 3.5), and there is no transition assistance, Content return or deletion obligation anywhere in the document. Alongside that, the § 12.1 licence to the Base Components is expressly revocable at IBM's discretion and does not reach our Affiliates or contractors; § 8.2(a)(3) requires us to indemnify IBM for Services Recipient claims relating to IBM's own Services; there is no conformance warranty for Materials or Base Components (which are provided "AS IS" under § 5.4(c)); and IBM carries no insurance obligation despite processing personal information on our behalf under § 14.18.

Second-tier items are the § 9 liability cap (mutual and fee-based, but with carve-outs limited to indemnities and bodily injury, and § 9.1(c)(2) excluding all liability for loss of our records or data), the Type II default ownership construct in § 7, the one-sided assignment restriction in § 14.10, the unlimited investigation right in § 11.3, and the 90-day non-renewal window with uncapped renewal pricing in § 3.2.

Note that § 3.4(b) early termination charges surface under two independently breached rules (T4C and LD); we should negotiate them once, as a single capped-fee-plus-refund package.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No exclusivity or sole-supplier covenant; § 14.11 (No Resale) is a scope limit, not a sourcing restriction. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.16 Freedom of Action | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restraint on our business. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | One month's notice is acceptable, but 3.4(b) charges are uncapped and § 3.5 gives no refund of prepaid Charges. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14.3 Choice of Law | New York law, no arbitration; venue is unstated — noted only. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 12.1 License | Grant is "revocable" and runs to Customer only; no Affiliate or contractor coverage. |
| Medium | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9.1 IBM's Limitation of Liability | Cap is mutual and fee-based, but no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct; § 9.1(c)(2) excludes data loss. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | No MFN in either direction. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 4.1 Charges | Charges follow Services actually ordered; no take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 14.8 Personnel | No no-hire or non-solicit covenant. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 3.5 Effect of Termination | § 3.5 addresses accrued payment only; no export, return or deletion right anywhere. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14.10 Assignment | Restricts Customer only; IBM is unrestricted and could assign to a competitor. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 11.3 Suspected Violations | Unlimited frequency, no notice of the investigation, no cost allocation, no bar on system access. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 8.1 Indemnification by IBM | IBM's IP indemnity meets the fallback; § 8.2(a)(3) makes us indemnify IBM for Services Recipient claims relating to IBM's Services. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14.19 Geographic Scope | No coverage obligation; § 14.12 allocates risk of loss only and § 5.3 is a disclaimer. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 5.4 Other Disclaimers | Type II is the § 7.a default; licence back is Enterprise-only with no modification or sublicensing; no Content/data ownership statement. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 3.4 Termination for Convenience | Uncapped early termination charges set outside the Agreement text (Attachment A / SOAs). |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | **Deviation** | § 3.2 Renewal | 90-day non-renewal window, renewal term mirrors the prior term, no price-uplift cap. |
| Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5.1 IBM Representations and Warranties | Services standard of care only; no conformance warranty, no warranty period, no remedy, and § 5.4(c) provides Materials "AS IS". |

---

## Walk-away items

These findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Revocable, Customer-only licence (§ 12.1)** — an at-will revocable grant with no Affiliate or contractor coverage is the rule's walk-away scenario; § 14.17 confirms nothing else cures it.
2. **No transition assistance or data return (§ 3.5)** — a hosting agreement with no right to retrieve our Content on exit. Preferred: six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter; 90 days' assistance is the fallback.
3. **Uncapped early termination charges (§ 3.4(b))** — an unquantified charge could reach or exceed remaining contract value, negating the convenience right. Fix: cap at three months' recurring Charges as the sole liquidated amount, plus pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges.
4. **Customer indemnity for IBM's own Services (§ 8.2(a)(3))** — the § 8.2(c) carve-back only reaches IBM bad faith, wilful misconduct, gross negligence or breach, leaving ordinary service-delivery claims with us. Narrow to our Content, Customer Components and our breach of applicable law.
5. **No deliverable warranty against an "AS IS" disclaimer (§ 5.1 / § 5.4(c))** — no conformance warranty, period or remedy. Add a 90-day conformance and no-malicious-code warranty and carve the express warranties out of § 5.4(c).
6. **No vendor insurance** — IBM operates the hosting environment and processes personal information on our behalf under § 14.18. Preferred package: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
7. **Unlimited, unannounced investigation right (§ 11.3)** — no frequency limit, no notice of the investigation itself, no bar on access to our systems.
8. **Auto-renewal mirroring the prior term (§ 3.2)** — a multi-year initial term under § 3.1 would produce automatic multi-year renewals on a 90-day window with no uplift cap.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline package** covering the eleven deviations and two missing clauses. Six proposals were verified as applied to the document text (LOL-CAP, ASSIGN, INSURANCE, LD, RENEWAL, WARRANTY); six did not verify on insertion (T4C, LICENSE, TRANSITION, AUDIT, INDEMN, IP) and need to be re-drafted and re-checked against the operative sections before the markup goes out.
2. **Bundle the exit package as one ask.** § 3.4(b) is flagged under both T4C and LD; negotiate a single provision capping early termination charges at three months' Charges as the sole liability and exclusive remedy, with pro-rata refund of prepaid Charges under § 3.5, and preserve the existing § 3.3 protection that IBM cannot recover these charges where IBM is the breaching party.
3. **Pair the transition clause with the licence fix.** Insert exit obligations into § 3.5, and in § 12.1 delete "revocable", tie licence termination to termination of the Agreement, and extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors. § 14.10 already handles successor transfer adequately.
4. **Add a single mutual Excluded Claims sentence to § 9** placing confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, and address the § 9.1(c)(2) exclusion of liability for loss of our records and data. The USD 100,000 floor and "paid" rather than "paid or payable" are secondary asks.
5. **Fix the § 7 IP default** to Type I, broaden the Type II licence back to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and add a Customer Content and data ownership statement. IBM's retained ownership of the Base Components (§§ 12.1, 12.3) is acceptable and should not be disturbed.
6. **Obtain Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments.** Early termination charges, Charges and renewal pricing all sit outside this text, so the exit-cost and renewal analysis cannot be closed without them.
7. **Fallbacks we can concede if pressed:** 90 days' transition assistance; 15 days' audit notice; 60-day non-renewal window with a 5% uplift cap; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M; Affiliates added on written notice under § 12.1.
8. **Note-only items (no redline unless the clause reopens):** add exclusive New York County venue to § 14.3; consider an MFN in our favour as a commercial ask; the additional preferred indemnity heads (breach of law, vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) beyond IBM's existing IP indemnity."}
